uniequip_002_ulpia:
'Laurentina, your outfit looks lovely today,' Blandus's voice comes through the glass of the partition. Laurentina turns with a smile and offers a quick 'thank you' as she gracefully leaves the lab. On the other side, Secunda suddenly stands up from behind the file shelf, staring intently at Ulpianus's back.
After a moment's hesitation, she speaks resolutely. 'Professor, I have a personal question.'
'Ask.' Ulpianus doesn't turn around.
'Why do you always wear the same clothes? You've been dressed like that since the day I met you.'
'Frankly, he's been dressing like that since he was a student. He's hardly changed his outfits at all over the years as I remember, and they always follow the same style, each more buttoned-up than the last. But I'd rather discourage such idle curiosity,' Blandus chimes in.
'Wrong question.' Ulpianus still doesn't turn around, his voice cold and firm.
'Understood!' Secunda answers brightly as she quickly leaves the lab.
Twenty minutes later, she reappears at the door.
'Professor, let me rephrase my question. Why do you rotate between dozens of outfits that look identical but differ slightly in material, craftsmanship, weight, and texture?'
'Still imprecise,' Ulpianus says, casting a quick glance at her before returning to his work sorting the mountain of Seaborn specimens.
Another twenty minutes pass, and Secunda appears again at the lab entrance, pen in hand.
'Professor, I've compared the differences in your outfits and analyzed the changes in your physical metrics, and I've found a preliminary correlation. Considering that combat gear aids Hunters in coordinating bodily movements, I hypothesize that you adjust details in your attire to match changes in your physical state, ensuring optimal control over your body in all conditions.'
After a brief silence, Ulpianus's ear moves slightly, as if signaling her to continue.
'However, this hypothesis leaves some gaps. Is there another variable influencing your choice of attire?'
'Indeed, Secunda.' Ulpianus finally turns around. 'You haven't noticed the correlation between the songs I compose pre-battle and my chosen outfit, but as those compositions have never been recorded, it's understandable you didn't realize this.'
'You mean, the other variable is...'
'My thoughts at the time.'
'Hold on!' At some point, Blandus had emerged from the partition. 'Ulpianus, that's not what you said when you explained it to me! You said it was because you didn't want to attract—'
'There are always more than one reason, Blandus.' Ulpianus cuts him off. 'What I told you was what you needed to know, and what I told her was what she needed to know. Nothing more.'
uniequip_003_ulpia:
It is pitch-black here, and the rocks all around the trench look exactly alike. He has been away from the city for too long; distant, glorious Aegir has become a tiny point of light behind him. The Seaborn before him gives off a faint glow. It swells its vesicles and extends soft tendrils, trying to grasp his arm, but he evades it. It seems not to know where to go, hovering in place, its faint glow blinking at a fixed rhythm. It spreads its pleated wing membranes, sensing the direction of the We-Many in the seawater. Then the Seaborn turns toward him and utters indistinct words, like clumsy Aegirian, calling to him, asking him to sense the direction of the We-Many together. It gurgles a few times and slowly calls him... "kin."
"I do not understand your way of communicating," he replies. "I am not one of you."
The Seaborn sways its limbs a few times. The guidance of the We-Many is unclear, and its glow dims somewhat. He sighs softly and instinctively feels the inner pocket of his clothes, drawing out a round piece of metal: a hydrocompass. He designed it himself, a purely mechanical construction that avoids any interference from the Seaborn. It was made specifically for the Abyssal Hunters, its function so simple as to be almost plain: at any time, to faithfully point the way home.
Yet the sensitive needle, which should swing quickly to discern its bearings, is stuck fast, pointing silently and stubbornly in one direction.

"How did it break? Smash against a rocky outcrop?" Brandus stares at the hydrocompass in his hand. "You should have chosen a higher-strength resin material in the first place." His old friend spreads his hands helplessly. "Abyssal Hunters issue. Every one of these little things that breaks is one fewer."
He wipes off the Seaborn tissue fluid splattered on his clothes. "No need to fix it." He reaches out and tucks the hydrocompass into his inner pocket, revealing an old wound on his forearm that has not fully healed. Brandus stares at the old wound, falls silent for a while, then speaks: "...'Researchers always come to resemble their results.' Has anyone ever said that to you?"
He calmly wipes away the blood from the reopened wound. "You really should have been a poet."
Brandus raises an eyebrow, accepts the retort, and goes on sorting the hunters' physical data. After a long while, the usually taciturn man rarely breaks the silence.
"...At least I can still move," he says.

The Seaborn seems to understand where to go now. Its tendrils wind around his arm, dragging him downward. He pulls his arm free, still standing his ground, and opens that hydrocompass one last time. It has long been broken and cracked, the old alloy stripped of its original luster. His name engraved on it is barely legible, yet the needle forever stubbornly points to Aegir. It has gone on too many missions with him and pointed the way to Aegir too many times, though his sense of direction is good enough: no matter how far away he is, he can always find his way home.
If our fates truly resemble each other this much... Ulpianus closes the lid of the hydrocompass and puts it back into his inner pocket. He pulls his collar closed, follows the Seaborn ahead, and heads into the deeper trench.
